newsitem.title: CANADA: Barrick discusses China joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Barrick discusses China joint venture.

text.p: Barrick Gold Corp is in the middle of discussions to form a joint venture in China, a spokesman said on Monday.
The gold miner is talking with Chinese government officials to put together a contract in the Kezhou area in Xinjiang province, Vince Borg said in a telephone interview.
Barrick has been involved in the area for about two years, collecting samples and doing geochemistry work, Borg said.
"We've got a number of blocks of land that we're looking at, exploring. All are in the early stages, grass roots exploration work."
Barrick needed to sign a joint venture contract if it wanted to move beyond preliminary exploration, Borg said.
China is the world's sixth biggest gold producer, but most of its mines are small, Borg added.
"They've got enormous potential," he said. "The mineral resources in the country are excellent."
China said earlier this month it was amending its mineral resources law to give foreign companies mining rights on Chinese soil.
Details were expected to be ready by the beginning of 1997.
